lyrics:
[Intro: rolling piano riff alone, bass joins]

[Verse 1: voice, piano and bass only]
She's got a duffel bag and a diner check
Born on the north shore of a town without a sea
He's got his father's coat and a one-way stare
Counting exits like a rosary

[Instrumental: lead guitar enters, climbing run, held note]

[Verse 2: drums enter, simple beat]
A radio plays in the laundromat
Somebody's quarters buying one more spin
Two strangers folding in fluorescent light
Both pretending they're not listening

[Pre-Chorus: guitar chug builds, harmonies appear]
Night owls, neon saints
Running on a rumor and a tank of maybe
One more town, one more try
The radio keeps saying "any day now, baby"

[Guitar Solo: melodic and lyrical]

[Verse 3: full band]
Now the years go by like mile signs
Some you read and some you miss
Everybody's got a window seat
And a name they tell the dark like this

[Pre-Chorus: builds with snare roll]
Night owls, neon saints
Running on a rumor and a tank of maybe
One more town, one more try
The radio keeps saying "any day now, baby"

[Chorus: first time, band wide open, big harmonies]
Keep the porch light on
I'm a long way out but I'm coming home
Keep the porch light on
Keep it burning 'til the dark is gone
Somebody, somewhere
Keep the porch light on

[Chorus: call and response]
Keep the porch light on
(Night owls) I can see it from the road
Keep the porch light on
(Neon saints) It's the only thing I know
Somebody, somewhere
Keep the porch light on

[Outro: title repeated, long fade out]
Keep the porch light on
Keep the porch light on
Keep the porch light on
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 118 BPM, 4/4, D major, built on a four-chord cycle that keeps rolling like wheels on a highway. Patient, cinematic and steadily rising.

VOICE: Soaring male tenor, clear and bright with effortless high notes and a slight cry at the top of phrases. Verses are sung like storytelling. The late chorus is delivered at full power with stacked three-part harmonies and answering backing lines.

INSTRUMENTS: Grand piano playing a rolling eighth-note riff with a walking left hand (the earworm). Electric bass doubling the piano's low notes. Palm-muted electric guitar that starts as a quiet chug and grows across the song. A lead guitar that plays fast ascending runs and singing sustained notes. Solid, simple arena drums. A shimmering string-synth pad joins late.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano riff alone for 4 bars, bass joins. 0:17 Verse 1, voice, piano and bass only. 0:50 Instrumental, lead guitar enters with a climbing run and a held note. 1:06 Verse 2, drums enter with a simple beat. 1:39 Pre-chorus 1, guitar chug doubles in intensity, harmonies appear. 1:55 Guitar solo, melodic and lyrical, quoting the pre-chorus tune. 2:16 Verse 3, full band. 2:48 Pre-chorus 2, builds with a snare roll. 3:05 Chorus, the title line arrives for the first time and the band is wide open. 3:30 Chorus repeat with call-and-response. 3:55 Outro, title repeated to a fade ending at 4:15 with no final chord.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Big, clean arena-rock polish. Piano bright and centred, guitars doubled and wide, snare with a roomy plate reverb, vocal crystal clear on top.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 3:05. After three minutes of waiting, the chorus finally lands. The delay is the design.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: A soft ambient pad and a sub-bass layer give modern depth. The fade is long and unresolved on purpose, so the song never ends, it just drives out of earshot.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Lonely, hopeful, then communal. One voice becomes a whole crowd.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Two strangers leaving nowhere towns cross paths in a late-night laundromat. Years roll by like mile signs. Everyone on the road is whispering the same request to someone back home.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a runaway calling home; a soldier or a touring musician; a grown child speaking to ageing parents; a prayer; or the voice of someone who has passed, asking to be remembered. For the listener who grew up in the 80s, it is also the kid you were, still on the way back.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: archetypes instead of names, cinematic night imagery, and the chorus held back until 3:05 so the first arrival is the climax. The 'wrong' geography is built in: 'the north shore of a town without a sea'. Designed mishearing: 'Keep the porch light on' will be sung as 'Keep the Porsche light on', which is the most 1980s mistake possible.
